newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK customs hopes for end to textile row with U.S.
newsitem.headline: HK customs hopes for end to textile row with U.S.

text.p: Hong Kong's customs chief expressed hope on Tuesday a long-running textile spat with the United States could end after U.S. custom agents completed their inspection of the colony's factories later this month.
"Before the end of this month, we will have a review of the situation with the American customs officers, who are already in Hong Kong," Customs and Excise Director Lawrence Li told reporters.
"We hope to be able to reach consensus and to persuade the United States to remove the additional import measures against us," he said.

Washington imposed rules last June requiring Hong Kong textile exporters to provide additional import documentation on a number of textile products in an attempt to stop illegal transshipments passing from China through Hong Kong to the United States.
Washington says manufacturers in China dodge quota limits by attaching false "Made In Hong Kong" labels.
A delegation from the U.S. Customs Service has been in Hong Kong since early January to evaluate the effectiveness of the territory's efforts to detect and prevent illegal transshipments.
"From what I have heard about the joint visit to the factories, the American customs officers are more satisfied than they were when they first came," Li said.
The customs chief also said Hong Kong had an adequate system to prevent transshipments, and that Washington should drop the stringent measures.
"Our control mechanism is adequate and we believe, with such a mechanism in place, the U.S. should not put in additional import requirements," he said.
